name: DA-MLDG
title: On efficacy of Meta-Learning for Domain Generalization in Speech Emotion Recognition
tagline: Why emotion models struggle beyond their training domain
summary: Models that recognize emotion in one speech dataset often fail on another. This study evaluates domain-shift-aware meta-learning for speech emotion recognition, finds mixed gains with log-mel inputs, and tests whether stronger acoustic representations improve held-out-domain performance.

figure.alt: Audio from multiple source domains is converted into spectrograms and divided into meta-train and meta-test sets; an energy-based domain shift margin adjusts the meta-test contribution.
figure.caption: Training repeatedly simulates a domain shift between source datasets. The estimated shift controls the influence of the meta-test loss when updating the shared emotion model.

method.title: Simulate unseen domains
method.text: Split source-domain batches into non-overlapping meta-train and meta-test sets. Take a training step on the meta-train set before evaluating transfer to the held-out source domains.

method.title: Estimate the domain shift
method.text: Compute the difference between average energy scores on the two sets after the meta-train step. This margin acts as an adaptive measure of the shift between domains.

method.title: Adapt the meta-objective
method.text: Weight the meta-test loss by the estimated shift and optimize it together with the meta-train loss. Evaluate transfer to target corpora that were unavailable during training.

findings.title: Modest gains, a persistent gap
findings.text: Across seven scenarios drawn from ten speech emotion datasets, domain-aware meta-learning gives modest improvements but does not solve generalization. The authors conclude that the resulting performance remains insufficient for practical use.

findings.title: Representation matters
findings.text: Replacing log-mel inputs with pre-trained TRILLsson embeddings improves results in several settings, including the supervised baseline. The study points to richer input representations and more varied in-the-wild data as priorities.

abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) refers to the recognition of human emotions from natural speech, vital for building human-centered context-aware intelligent systems. Here, domain shift, where models’ trained on one domain exhibit performance degradation when exposed to an unseen domain with different statistics, is a major limiting factor in SER applicability, as models have a strong dependence on speakers and languages characteristics used during training. Meta-Learning for Domain Generalization (MLDG) has shown great success in improving models’ generalization capacity and alleviate the domain shift problem in the vision domain; yet, its’ efficacy on SER remains largely unexplored. In this work, we propose a “domain-shift aware” MLDG approach to learn generalizable models across multiple domains in SER. Based on our extensive evaluation, we identify a number of pitfalls that contribute to poor models’ DG ability, and demonstrate that log-mel spectrograms representations lack distinct features required for MLDG in SER. We further explore the use of appropriate features to achieve DG in SER as to provide insides to future research directions for DG in SER.
